“In 1889 and 1890 the entire northwestern quarter of the United States—the Dakotas, Montana, Wyoming, Idaho, and Washington—ceased to be territories and became states of the Union. In every state and territory Anglo-Americans and their culture predominated, making a very different region from 1848. The Census Bureau in its introduction to the 1890 census stated that no meaningful frontier line—meaning a Western line of settlement—could be mapped any longer.” (Walter Nugent,Into the West: The Story of Its People[New York: Alfred A.
